---
title: "CSIL History Archive"
subtitle: "A public evidence archive for Choice in Supports for Independent Living in British Columbia"
toc: false
---

Choice in Supports for Independent Living (CSIL) is the name of a British Columbia home-support program. Public program materials describe it as a way for eligible people to manage funding and employ their own workers. This site does not treat those program descriptions as a substitute for historical evidence about how CSIL was designed, piloted, or changed.

This archive exists to collect, cite, and annotate the sources from which a history of CSIL can be reconstructed. It is meant for CSIL employers, disability advocates, researchers, journalists, policy staff, and people who took part in that history. The project is a digital-history and annotated-bibliography effort, not a campaign.

The reconstruction is incomplete on purpose. Pages distinguish documented fact, attributed recollection, interpretation, conflicting evidence, and open questions. Where dates or lineages are still unsettled — including whether later writers treat **1993 or 1994** as a CSIL starting year, and how that relates to a later official **1994 pilot / 1995 province-wide** pairing — the archive shows the disagreement rather than hiding it.

A working research proposition used only to organise this site, and **not** offered here as a settled history, is:

**institutional or agency care → disability-led independent-living experiments → Creekview → Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM) → direct individualized funding → CSIL design and pilot → a province-wide program.**

Cited chapters now reconstruct Creekview (and the folded origins/context), ECPM, CSIL design/pilot, and later evolution from public sources. None of those chapters treats Creekview → ECPM → CSIL as a proven formal succession. A short [state of the evidence](history/index.qmd#state-of-the-evidence) summary lives on the History index.

If you can help, the most useful contributions are citations, catalogue records, permitted scans, and corrections. Please read [About / Contribute](about.qmd#how-to-contribute) and do not send private or health-related records.
